title: Harness-first local coding swarm locked acceptance matrix

scope.execution: real local storage, filesystem, recursive agents, git facade, approved subprocesses, and terminal
scope.sandbox_boundary: An execution-provider boundary is preserved; workspace routing is not process confinement.

entries.contract: The implementation is isolated in the managed codex/graphcoder-sdk worktree from the pinned SDK commit, with no merge into the source checkout.
entries.verification: worktree provenance and git ancestry audit

entries.contract: Q:\graphcoder is read-only reference material; no source or generated artifact is copied from it into the SDK implementation.
entries.verification: source-boundary audit

entries.contract: Models are mocked while storage, filesystem, recursion, git facade, approved process execution, and terminal interaction are real.
entries.verification: real-effects swarm scenario with deterministic model fixture

entries.contract: No sandbox is implemented; the execution-provider boundary remains explicit and workspace routing is not described as confinement.
entries.verification: boundary and dependency audit

entries.contract: Cloud, web UI components, historical migration, and production model adapters stay outside this local goal while the wrapper remains usable in terminal and native hosts.
entries.verification: scope and dependency audit

entries.contract: Harness owns one versioned model-request construction path with an ordered input manifest, component revisions, content references, and digest.
entries.verification: serialized provider request capture and manifest equality

entries.contract: Only the pinned prompt, tool definitions, authoritative conversation, declared workspace instructions, explicitly requested content, and delivered messages enter model input.
entries.verification: provider capture excludes hidden retrieval, UI state, sibling history, and summaries

entries.contract: Message order, roles, content bytes, tool-call identities, and result pairing are preserved exactly.
entries.verification: Unicode, whitespace, attachment, call/result byte comparison

entries.contract: Tool arguments and results are validated against their pinned schemas before model admission.
entries.verification: malformed call, invalid argument, invalid result, and missing-content cases

entries.contract: Workspace content is generation-pinned and historical references are never resolved through mutable current paths.
entries.verification: content-generation mutation and stale-reference replay

entries.contract: Transport metadata and runtime credentials stay outside model-visible content and model-input construction.
entries.verification: serialized request inspection and credential-free environment audit

entries.contract: Context and output limits are explicit; overflow produces a typed outcome without silent truncation or summarization.
entries.verification: oversized request, output, attachment, and render cases

entries.contract: Forks use the existing Harness fork path and pin the parent authoritative conversation and workspace at one consistent boundary.
entries.verification: production fork-tool boundary scenario

entries.contract: A child inherited model-input prefix is byte-perfect, including prompt, tool-definition revisions, conversation content, calls, results, attachments, and instructions.
entries.verification: parent/child serialized prefix byte comparison

entries.contract: The triggering fork tool exchange is complete and paired in both parent and child histories before the child request is constructed.
entries.verification: fork call/result ordering and orphan rejection

entries.contract: Fork notification, child task, identity/workspace information, and fresh private scratch context occur strictly after the shared prefix.
entries.verification: suffix ordering and fresh-scratch generation assertions

entries.contract: Recursive forks at several depths retain every ancestor prefix exactly and exclude later parent changes.
entries.verification: three-level recursive prefix replay after parent mutation

entries.contract: Fork prefixes and immutable serialization references survive restart and cannot be reinterpreted.
entries.verification: close/reopen prefix digest and reference replay

entries.contract: Child permissions are separately scoped; transcript inheritance does not grant mutable state access.
entries.verification: cross-agent grant and private-state denial cases

entries.contract: Running subprocesses and unfinished effects are not cloned during a fork.
entries.verification: interrupted-effect fork admission and process identity audit

entries.contract: Parallel fork batches have one completed boundary and ordered results before any child model request; no orphan call or fabricated result is admitted.
entries.verification: simultaneous-child batch barrier and fault injection

entries.contract: Every mutation and process execution enters Harness admission with policy, operation identity, and durable effect recording.
entries.verification: journal inspection for every effect kind

entries.contract: Invalid, unauthorized, stale, or incorrectly scoped operations are rejected before execution.
entries.verification: typed admission denials with executor invocation counters

entries.contract: Admission is durable before dispatch and observed outcome is durable before success is exposed.
entries.verification: crash points before dispatch and after execution

entries.contract: Interrupted effects reconcile by stable operation identity and retry only when the provider guarantee permits it.
entries.verification: at-most-once, exactly-once, and idempotent recovery matrix

entries.contract: Unknown subprocess outcomes remain uncertain and are never rerun automatically.
entries.verification: process disconnect/crash after dispatch

entries.contract: Cancellation, timeout, denied, failed, and uncertain outcomes remain in durable history.
entries.verification: terminal cancellation and journal outcome replay

entries.contract: Conflicting workspace publications serialize and stale operations are fenced by owner and generation.
entries.verification: concurrent publication and stale-writer race

entries.contract: Arbitrary host commands require approval bound to exact executable, arguments, working directory, and environment policy; approved environments do not inherit credentials.
entries.verification: command-policy positive/negative matrix and environment capture

entries.contract: Children fork their direct parent pinned workspace with fresh private scratch; siblings remain isolated.
entries.verification: root/two-child/grandchild real filesystem scenario

entries.contract: Only a direct parent may integrate or discard a child; descendants move upward one level at a time.
entries.verification: authorized and unauthorized merge/discard operations

entries.contract: Workspace integration preserves conflict resolution, merge continuation, abort, rebase, discard, and recovery semantics.
entries.verification: overlapping-edit conflict scenario with restart at each continuation state

entries.contract: Bare Git remains distinct from the acyclic git facade, whose commands invoke typed SDK operations under caller authority.
entries.verification: facade boundary and dependency audit

entries.contract: Root checkout changes are held until an approval bound to the exact writeback operation is granted.
entries.verification: root writeback approval and pre-approval checkout digest

entries.contract: Concurrent user edits survive writeback reconciliation without stale overwrite.
entries.verification: user-edit race with three-way reconciliation

entries.contract: Model-facing tools include read, edit, search, execute, fork, message, and wait with pinned schemas.
entries.verification: tool-definition manifest and invocation contract tests

entries.contract: Fork creates a recursively capable child with a task and bounded resource allocation.
entries.verification: model-facing fork scenario and allocation ledger

entries.contract: Message delivers explicit content to an authorized target without splicing another transcript into model input.
entries.verification: delivery identity/order/replay and sibling-transcript exclusion

entries.contract: Wait observes specified agents or messages with durable cancellation and timeout behavior.
entries.verification: restartable wait matrix with deadline and cancellation

entries.contract: Completion publishes an agent outcome and changeset without automatically merging it.
entries.verification: completion and pending-integration inspection

entries.contract: Git-facade operations expose status, diff, commit, merge, rebase, and discard through typed authority checks.
entries.verification: facade command matrix against real workspaces

entries.contract: Invalid targets, unauthorized integrations, malformed calls, and resource-limit violations produce typed results and never dispatch effects.
entries.verification: negative tool and integration matrix with executor counters

entries.contract: Active-agent, total-agent, recursion-depth, model-step, output, and execution-time limits are configurable and enforced.
entries.verification: one-negative-case-per-limit with typed results

entries.contract: Descendants cannot allocate beyond the session remaining budget.
entries.verification: nested allocation race and persisted remaining-budget audit

entries.contract: Harness owns orchestration, model-input construction, forks, communication, policy, and recovery; Filesystem owns workspace behavior; host adapters own platform execution.
entries.verification: dependency-boundary source audit

entries.contract: A durable local composition constructor supplies journals, readers, grants, and recovery without manual application assembly.
entries.verification: constructor reopen/resume integration

entries.contract: The terminal app supports starting, reopening, and resuming sessions.
entries.verification: installed-artifact headless and PTY session lifecycle

entries.contract: The terminal app supports input, agent-tree/activity inspection, messages, approvals, cancellation, change inspection, and root-writeback approval.
entries.verification: interactive scripted PTY scenario

entries.contract: Interactive and headless operation use the same generic UI state and event logic, suitable for native apps.
entries.verification: headless/PTY event transcript parity

entries.contract: Mock fixture selection is explicit and visible in the session descriptor.
entries.verification: fixture selection and request provenance inspection

entries.contract: GraphCoder is a small composition and entrypoint wrapper with no independent orchestration or storage semantics.
entries.verification: GraphCoder dependency and source audit

entries.contract: Session listing and inspection lazy-load history pages, file bodies, diffs, and optional execution integrations.
entries.verification: instrumented request/load counters

entries.contract: Listing sessions does not start workers or fetch entire workspaces.
entries.verification: worker-start and workspace-read counters during listing

entries.contract: Changed public contracts have generated TypeScript bindings owned by Rust definitions.
entries.verification: generation and clean generated-tree check

entries.contract: Supported native and WASM serializations agree on public contract semantics.
entries.verification: native/WASM round-trip and negative-case parity

entries.contract: A root agent forks two children and one child forks a grandchild through the production runtime.
entries.verification: mock-driven recursive swarm scenario

entries.contract: Agents perform real edits, communicate, wait, inspect diffs, and complete with durable outcomes.
entries.verification: recursive swarm activity transcript and filesystem assertions

entries.contract: Grandchild changes integrate grandchild-to-child-to-root and produce exact final files.
entries.verification: ordered integration and final-byte assertions

entries.contract: Overlapping edits exercise conflict resolution, continuation, abort, rebase, and discard.
entries.verification: real filesystem conflict matrix

entries.contract: Sibling merges and grandchild-to-root merges are rejected with typed authorization outcomes.
entries.verification: negative integration matrix

entries.contract: Discard, rebase, cancellation, resource limits, and denied operations are observable and recoverable.
entries.verification: scripted swarm control matrix

entries.contract: Faults before admission, after admission, during execution, after execution before result persistence, and during fork/merge publication recover without false success.
entries.verification: fault-injection matrix at every named boundary

entries.contract: Recovery causes no duplicate fork, message, publication, or unsafe effect replay and preserves the original model-input prefix.
entries.verification: restart/disconnect replay and identity audit

entries.contract: Rust, generated bindings, TypeScript contracts, provider conformance, Filesystem/plugin regressions, package consumption, and dependency-boundary checks run against the final source.
entries.verification: qualification lane receipt

entries.contract: Windows native E2E is distinguished from compilation; platform execution evidence is retained for each required platform lane.
entries.verification: native execution and compile-only lane audit

entries.contract: Every result records source, suite, descriptor, and artifact digests; required failures, skips, missing evidence, and flaky cases block final completion.
entries.verification: receipt schema and final-gate validator
